rv.q: It’s life and time and family abstracted, distilled and theatricalized with a spare yet rich minimalism.
Now, in a lovely revival for TUTA under the direction of Jacqueline Stone for the second year, The Long Christmas Dinner reminds us that the holidays are a time for celebration and remembrance.
This show brings that lesson home, with a lovely delicacy of touch.
It’s still a fine, thought-provoking piece of theatre and a welcome antidote to the schmaltz of the season.
Thornton Wilder’s “The Long Christmas Dinner”, directed by Jacqueline Stone, offers a sobering counterpoint to the usual cheer of the season.

cn.t: Critics praise this "gem" of a Wilder one-act as a quietly powerful meditation on family and mortality spanning 90 years of Christmas dinners, though less known than "Our Town," it resonates as a sobering seasonal counterpoint.
